source.title: Similar Models Learn Differently: Final-Window Pretraining Shapes Post-Training Beyond SFT
source.authors: Cen Lu; Yung-Chen Tang; Andrea Cavallaro

record.tranche_reason: The study examines refusal erosion after different pretraining and post-training paths, and uses a refusal-direction projection probe as a mechanism diagnostic. It does not test the difference-in-means direction by ablating or adding it, nor does it test the claim versions about direction-mediated refusal.
record.gate_note: The study reports refusal erosion under DPO and GRPO, but these are outcomes of changing training data or post-training, not interventions on the claimed direction. The authors say a refusal-direction projection probe did not cleanly separate Cweb and Csafety; the text gives no numerical probe result or further method detail.
record.test_reason: The study measures how much refusal survives DPO or GRPO after different final pretraining windows. It cites Arditi et al. only for a refusal-direction projection probe in Appendix F, which it reports qualitatively as not separating the branches. No direction is ablated, added, weight-edited or tested for transfer. V7 concerns whether training decides that one removable direction exists; this study varies training but never checks for such a direction, so it does not test V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. Additions: the effect is selective to safety-transformation text, fades as the window shrinks relative to prior training, and replicates on Pythia-1B. The authors say the protection costs over-refusal and about 0.9 points of capability. They urge reporting what a model was trained on last. The probe is described only as not cleanly separating the branches, a minor appendix diagnostic.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies final-window pretraining and evaluates refusal erosion under DPO and GRPO; it does not find a harmful-minus-harmless mean-activation direction and ablate or add it.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported refusal-erosion effect varies with final-window content and order, relative window size, post-training recipe, preference data, model family, and benchmark.

fits_no_version.finding: On OLMo-2-1B, a 500M-token safety-text final pretraining window cuts refusal erosion under the same DPO (overall 24.0 vs 32.2 pp) and GRPO (6.1 vs 16.9 pp) versus web text, from matched post-SFT refusal. The effect requires safety text to come last, fades at small relative dose, and replicates on Pythia-1B. A refusal-direction projection probe did not separate the branches.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Final-window pretraining content and order affect how much SFT-installed refusal survives later post-training; this resistance is not visibly reflected in a refusal-direction projection.

record.problems: The direction-projection diagnostic is described only qualitatively and does not cleanly distinguish the branches. Most refusal-erosion outcomes are not interventions on the direction named in the claim; the main controlled experiments use 1B models.
record.rows_left_out: Not applicable; all extracted rows are within the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: No ablation or addition of a difference-in-means direction; no measure of refusal removal, induction or capability retention under intervention.
No jailbreak or adversarial-training analysis tied to the direction.
No comparison of single, affine or cone accounts.
No separation of harm judgment from refusal in representations. WildGuard harm scores are outputs, not internal encodings.
No direction transfer. The Pythia replication is of the erosion effect, not of a direction.
Training content and order change refusal erosion, but whether one removable direction exists is never tested.

record.verdict_notes: Rows r1–r18 measure refusal erosion under training. They correctly have versions ['none']. No verdicts are given because no version is tested. Additional erosion results (Pythia Table 13, Chatbot Arena Table 14, Base Table 11, dose attenuation) are not rows. They do not bear on any version, so they are not listed as missing.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means direction is ablated or added; the study does not measure whether such an intervention removes or induces refusal, or preserves other abilities.
No direction ablation is converted into a weight edit or evaluated as abliteration.
No attack is tested for suppressing the direction, and no training against its ablation is evaluated.
The study does not compare affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts of refusal.
The study does not separate a harmfulness judgment from a refusal decision.
No direction-transfer test across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models is conducted.
The study varies final-window pretraining content and order and measures refusal erosion, but does not test whether these choices determine whether a single removable direction exists.
